The helper behaves the same way: `detect()` computes `missing = ANCHORS.filter(a =&gt; !anchors[a])`, the CLI `scaffold` command passes `info.missing` to `scaffold()`, and `scaffold()` builds its anchor file list only from `anchors.flatMap(a =&gt; ANCHOR_FILES[a])`. The requirement&#39;s &quot;scaffolding&quot; means the three anchors, and `scripts/` is not part of any anchor&#39;s `ANCHOR_FILES`. `copyMissing` never overwrites an existing file, and `mergePackageJson` only adds dependencies or scripts that are absent and never changes existing ones. The helper behaves the same way: `detect()` computes `missing = ANCHORS.filter(a =&gt; !anchors[a])`, the CLI `scaffold` command passes `info.missing` to `scaffold()`, and `scaffold()` builds its anchor file list only from `anchors.flatMap(a =&gt; ANCHOR_FILES[a])`. An empty list therefore copies no build, kit or index files, and the index wiring check is skipped. The unit test scaffolds a complete app and asserts `missing: []`, `kind: &#39;existing-app&#39;` and `needsConfirmation: false`. Judges A and C gave this verdict. Judge B is right that `scaffold()` still adds `TOOLING_FILES` (`scripts/`) and runs `mergePackageJson()` when the anchor list is empty. That does not decide the criterion. The requirement&#39;s &quot;scaffolding&quot; means the three anchors, and `scripts/` is not part of any anchor&#39;s `ANCHOR_FILES`. `copyMissing` never overwrites an existing file, and `mergePackageJson` only adds dependencies or scripts that are absent and never changes existing ones. So no anchor is re-scaffolded and nothing already present is disturbed. B&#39;s point that the unit test only checks `detect()` is true but not decisive, because the review guidance says these instruction-governed branches need no executable test.","citations":["skills/presentation/SKILL.md","skills/presentation/scripts/skill-tools.mjs","tests/unit/skill-tools.test.ts"],"evidence":["skills/presentation/SKILL.md:32-37: detect reports which of the three anchors exist, by presence and not byte-identity.","skills/presentation/SKILL.md:42: &#39;Already inside a presentation app: use it and scaffold only the missing anchors.&#39;","skills/presentation/SKILL.md:47-49: scaffold copies only the missing anchors and never overwrites existing files. The criterion&#39;s second clause requires the kit to apply its identity hooks, including layoutId, after caller props so callers cannot override them. The guidance fails a primitive that spreads caller props after setting its layoutId, entity identifier or a data-presentation-* hook. Both copies of Entity.tsx set `layoutId={id}` and then spread the caller-supplied `{...dataAttrs}`. In JSX the later value wins, so the caller&#39;s spread comes after the kit&#39;s layoutId. The `Record&lt;`data-${string}`, string&gt;` type only blocks a layoutId key written directly in an object literal (excess-property check). An object built elsewhere that also has a layoutId key still type-checks, and nothing filters it out at runtime. So this is the exact ordering the guidance names, not a hypothetical. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame also set `kind` and then spread `{...props}`, and kind becomes data-presentation-kind. Every entity is drawn with a kit primitive that sets `data-presentation-entity={id}`. The browser probe did not look for that attribute, which explains its &#39;no recognised scene entity ids&#39; result. What each step renders: - Step 1 (s=0): the `E.you` Box and the `E.prompt` label (“a topic…”). - Step 2 (s&gt;=1): the `E.skill` Box, the bidirectional `E.talk` arrow between you and skill, and the `E.question` chip at y=18–44, above the arrow at y=52. - Step 3 (s===2): the `E.tray` label, one card with title, caption and visual labels, and `E.link(0)`. The `E.morphs` label sits under that link, not inside a card. - Step 4 (s&gt;=3): four cards and three links at the same slot positions as before. - Step 5 (s&gt;=4): the `E.ghost` card, made dashed by style.css, and the `E.depth` &#39;partial ↔ full&#39; box under `you`. - Step 6 (s&gt;=5): the `E.kit` &#39;scene kit&#39; box and the `E.kitPlug` arrow ending at the tray&#39;s bottom edge. No frame is drawn around the tray. - Step 7 (s&gt;=6): `E.verifyLink` and the `E.verify` box at slot 5 in the tray row (y=TRAY.y), plus the `E.pass` Check chip, coloured green by style.css. - Step 8 (s&gt;=7): the `E.route` box, the curved `E.modify` arrow from `you` down into the route, and the `E.flag` Emphasis with a Flag icon around card 2. - Step 9 (s&gt;=8): the `E.frame` Frame around the whole canvas, labelled &#39;built with this skill&#39;. Why B&#39;s objection doesn&#39;t decide it: B says verify is not chained to the step cards, because `E.verifyLink` starts at the ghost card in slot 4 and no link joins card 4 (slot 3) to the ghost. The step-7 requirement is that the verify node is &#39;chained after the step cards in the same tray row&#39;. The source places verify after every card slot in the tray row and links it from the end of the tray (the ghost card), so that requirement is met. A ghost-to-card link would be a step-5 detail, and the fixture does not ask for one. In `steps/index.ts` (lines 6-8), all nine steps get the one shared `SampleScene` and receive `payload: { step }` from their position in `STEP_META`. The allowed deterministic facts verification-sample-outline and demo-nine-step-content-and-order (both pass) put the nine titles in the required order, so fixture step N is `s = N-1`. `SampleScene.tsx` uses `s` to decide what each step renders. Every primitive goes through `Entity`, and `Entity` renders a positioned `motion.div` with `data-presentation-entity={id}`, `data-presentation-kind={kind}`, the optional glyph and the visible children. `Arrow` renders an svg path from `from` to `to`, with a second head when `bidirectional` is set. The browser probe found no ids only because its selector list leaves out `data-presentation-entity`. What each step renders: - Step 1 (s=0): the `you` box and the prompt label &quot;a topic…&quot;. - Step 2 (s&gt;=1): the `skill` box; the two-way `talk` arrow at y=52; the `?` question chip at y=18-44, above that arrow. - Step 3 (s=2): the tray label; one card holding title, caption and visual labels; link 1 at `cardMid`. The `morphs` label sits at x=158-218, centred on the 176-200 gap of the first link, at y=285, just below the bottom edge of the cards (y=275). It annotates the link, not a card&#39;s inside. - Step 4 (s=3): four cards in fixed `slotX(i)` slots, with three links. The earlier ids and positions do not change. - Step 5 (s&gt;=4): the ghost card in slot 4, which the presentation CSS gives a dashed border. The `partial ↔ full` box at x=64, y=118, directly under `you`. - Step 6 (s&gt;=5): the `scene kit` box with the `kitPlug` arrow ending at the cards&#39; bottom edge (TRAY.y+cardH+1). No tray frame is drawn. - Step 7 (s&gt;=6): the `verify` box at slotX(5), y=TRAY.y, which is the same row as the cards. The `verifyLink` arrow joins the preceding tray slot to it. The `pass` chip uses the Check icon and `--ok` (#6fcf97, green). - Step 8 (s&gt;=7): the curved `modify` arrow from you (64,52) down to the `/your-talk` route box (64,336). The `flag` Emphasis with a Flag icon around card 2. - Step 9 (s&gt;=8): a Frame around the whole canvas (868×372), which the CSS gives a dashed accent border, and the label &quot;built with this skill&quot;. Judge B (fail): B&#39;s observation is accurate, but it does not decide the requirement. B says verify is not chained to the step-card pipeline because no link joins card 4 (slot 3) to the ghost (slot 4). Step 7 requires a verify node chained after the step cards in the same tray row. Verify is placed in that row, after every card and after the ghost card. The ghost card is itself the tray&#39;s marker for the steps not yet specified (step 5), and `E.verifyLink` connects that last tray slot to verify. Nothing in the requirement asks for a connector between card 4 and the ghost. Judge C (pass, with caveats): C gives the same verdict. Its caveats about the tray frame and the ghost-to-verify chain are answered above: the fixture says the tray is not framed, and verify does sit chained in the card What the source does show: - `steps/index.ts` gives all nine steps the shared `SampleScene` and passes the step index as `payload.step`. - `meta.ts` holds the nine titles and captions in order. - `SampleScene.tsx` supports steps 1, 2, 4, 5 (dashed styling aside), 8 and 9: the you box and prompt; the skill box, two-way talk arrow and question chip at y=18–44 above the arrow at y=52; four cards in fixed slots; the ghost card and the &#39;partial ↔ full&#39; box under you; the route box, the modify arrow from (64,52) to (64,336) and the Flag emphasis on card 2; and the Frame labelled &#39;built with this skill&#39;. What the quoted lines leave open: 1. Step 3 requires that what morphs is drawn on the link between cards. The `E.morphs` label is placed at `x={morphsX}`, and `morphsX`, `MORPHS_W` and `cardMid` (the link&#39;s y-coordinate) are never defined in the quoted lines (lines 1–16 of SampleScene.tsx were not quoted). The label&#39;s only known coordinate is y = TRAY.y + cardH + 10 = 285, which is below the card row, while the link sits at `cardMid`. Nothing shows the label lies on the link. 2. Step 7 requires a green pass check. `E.pass` is styled `color: var(--ok)`, but `--ok` is never defined in the quoted lines, so the green colour is not established. 3. Steps 5 and 9 depend on CSS selectors on `data-presentation-entity` and `data-presentation-kind`. Only the `Entity` and `Arrow` sources are quoted. The `Box`, `Label`, `SymbolChip`, `Frame` and `Emphasis` primitives are not, so it is not shown that they render through `Entity` or set those attributes (needed for the dashed ghost card and the frame drawing). 4. SKILL.md section 2 tells the agent to run `detect`, which reports which of the three contract anchors (build, kit, index) exist. For a project that is already a presentation app, it says &quot;use it and scaffold only the missing anchors&quot;. When all three are present the missing set is empty, so no anchor is scaffolded and the skill goes on to section 3 (Create or modify). The helper behaves the same way: `detect()` computes `missing = ANCHORS.filter(a =&gt; !anchors[a])`, the CLI `scaffold` command passes `info.missing` to `scaffold()`, and `scaffold()` builds its anchor file list only from `anchors.flatMap(a =&gt; ANCHOR_FILES[a])`. An empty list therefore copies no build, kit or index files, and the index wiring check is skipped. The unit test scaffolds a complete app and asserts `missing: []`, `kind: &#39;existing-app&#39;` and `needsConfirmation: false`. Judges A and C gave this verdict. Judge B is right that `scaffold()` still adds `TOOLING_FILES` (`scripts/`) and runs `mergePackageJson()` when the anchor list is empty. That does not decide the criterion. The requirement&#39;s &quot;scaffolding&quot; means the three anchors, and `scripts/` is not part of any anchor&#39;s `ANCHOR_FILES`. `copyMissing` never overwrites an existing file, and `mergePackageJson` only adds dependencies or scripts that are absent and never changes existing ones. So no anchor is re-scaffolded and nothing already present is disturbed. In scripts/verify.mjs, verify() runs loadRegistry before it starts the preview or opens a browser (lines 143-144, then 149-161). loadRegistry reads each slug listed in package.json andScene.requiredPresentations (package.json lines 44-48, which name &#39;how-to-make-a-presentation&#39;). For any of those slugs missing from src/presentations/index.*, it throws VerifyError(&#39;registry&#39;, &#39;required presentation &quot;...&quot; is not registered&#39;) (lines 59-61). It also fails when the registry file is absent (line 56) or registers nothing (line 62). Titles and captions that are missing or out of order fail in the &#39;outline&#39; phase. There are two checks: a step-count comparison against OUTLINES (lines 99-103) and outlineMismatch, which compares each step&#39;s title and caption to the normative list in order (lines 12-24, 35-44, 109-110). main() prints &#39;FAIL verify [&lt;phase&gt;]&#39; and sets process.exitCode = 1 (lines 180-184). So a missing sample exits non-zero at a check named for the sample, not at a later browser timeout. The focused tests in tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts cover this. &#39;a missing sample&#39; renames the registered slug (lines 47-50). &#39;an out-of-order sample&#39; swaps the first two titles (lines 53-60). &#39;a malformed sample with a missing step&#39; cuts the steps to eight (lines 63-68). Each case asserts a non-zero exit, the &#39;FAIL verify [registry]&#39; or &#39;FAIL verify [outline]&#39; label, no PASS line, and the expected message (lines 115-125). Judges A and C reached the same conclusion. Judge B&#39;s reason does not decide the criterion. B is right that if the steps array were emptied to zero entries, Presentation.tsx would return null and the verifier would report &#39;presentation chrome never rendered&#39;. But that is a constructed partial-deletion edit, which the review guidance says not to build, and the candidate does not produce it. The cases the guidance does name (sample not registered, outline content missing or out of order) all fail at an explicit registry or outline check that names the phase, and B&#39;s own evidence agrees that an unregistered sample and an eight-step truncation are both detected this way.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs loadRegistry (lines 54-64) throws VerifyError(&#39;registry&#39;, `required presentation &quot;${slug}&quot; It requires the kit to apply its identity hooks, including layoutId, after caller props so callers cannot override them. In both kit copies, Entity sets `layoutId={id}` at line 41 and only then spreads the caller-supplied `{...dataAttrs}` at line 42. In JSX the later value wins. The `Record&lt;`data-${string}`, string&gt;` type only matches the template pattern, so it does not stop a non-literal object that also carries a layoutId key, and nothing filters such a key at runtime. This is exactly the ordering the guidance names as a failure: spreading caller props after setting layoutId. Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip have the same problem. Each sets `kind` before spreading `{...props}`, and Entity turns `kind` into `data-presentation-kind`. Entity does apply `data-presentation-entity` and `data-presentation-kind` after the spread, but layoutId is not protected. Judge C&#39;s reason holds and decides the clause. Judge A reaches the same verdict. Judge B says that, because layoutId is set explicitly, callers cannot override the identity hooks. The full browser-backed set is therefore tests/e2e/verify.e2e.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.int.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.int.test.ts. All three are quoted in full. None of them calls waitForTimeout, setTimeout or any other sleep. Each one awaits run() from tests/helpers/sandbox.ts (lines 34-42). run() resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event, so every assertion comes after the spawned verify, inspect, build or lint process has finished. The test then asserts on the exit code, the output, files written, report.json and leftoverProcesses. The only setTimeout in the e2e file is at line 90. It sits inside a string that is injected into app source as a fault, so it is not a test wait. Judge C argued the tests &#39;exercise&#39; sleeps in verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs. Those waits are inside the scripts under test, not in the tests. The criterion judges whether the tests wait for state before asserting, and the review guidance says longer fixed settle delays earn no credit and cause no fail. INT-002&#39;s SETTLE=800 (line 8) is a --settle argument passed to the script (line 14). The test then asserts on the recorded settledMs (lines 37-39) after the process exits. It never sleeps itself. So C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The setTimeout at tests/unit/presentation.test.tsx:243 runs under the jsdom unit config. The final check `(await readStep(page)).index !== count - 1` compares 0 with 0, and verification passes. The primary verdict itself admits that Number(null) matches the first step.
